Let $B=[\begin{aligned}2x+1 & x-40 \\ 1 & -x\end{aligned}]$
be a singular matrix. **In ascending order**, the values of $x$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =(2x+1)\cdot (-x)-(x-40)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-x-x+40 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-2x+40.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-2x+40 & =0 \\ -2({x}^{2}+x-20) & =0 \\ -2(x-4)(x+5) & =0 \\ x & =4,-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $x$ are

$$
x=-5\,\text{and}\,x=4.
$$
